title: kv-cache: adaptive compaction & spillover eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Asha Patel
body: Context: production clusters have seen increased KV-cache fragmentation and a growing incidence of OOMs when models with long context windows and many concurrent streams are served. Current spillover + eviction logic prioritizes LRU-like recency but does not account for memory fragmentation and cross-tenant entitlement, which causes inefficient paging and repeated re-population of hot kv-shards. Motivation: reduce tail latency and OOM frequency by (1) adding an adaptive in-place compaction/auto-coalescing pass, (2) introducing an eviction priority that considers fragmentation score and page residency, and (3) introducing a lightweight background pager that moves cold pages to host spill files more predictably. Summary of changes: - Runtime: add compactor module that tracks chunk fragmentation, coalesces adjacent free ranges, and compacts low-activity shards when fragmentation>threshold. - Evictor: new scoring function combining age, last-access-span, fragmentation-score, and estimated re-population cost. - Spillover pager: background thread (configurable rate) that serializes cold pages to spill store with async prefetch metadata to reduce miss penalty. - Scheduler integration: eviction/compaction work is scheduled on a separate IO/maintenance pool to avoid interfering with token-serving threads; work stealing limited to non-critical queues. - Config knobs: compaction_threshold, compaction_rate_limit, eviction_fragmentation_weight, spill_prefetch_window, pager_io_budget. - Tests/benchmarks: added unit tests for compaction correctness, integration bench harness that simulates mixed short/long context workloads, and end-to-end latency/cost benchmarks. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag kv.compaction.enabled=false by default; gradual rollout to Dedicated and Hosted low-traffic pools with telemetry. Considerations: this PR focuses on memory layout heuristics and the background pager; it intentionally avoids changing quantization or model kernel paths to narrow scope. If enabled aggressively, compaction can increase CPU/IO spend; default config aims to keep overhead <1% p99 latency impact while reducing OOMs and tail misses.
commits:
1) Initial compactor and fragmentation scoring (asha/compactor)
2) Evictor: new priority function + metrics (asha/evictor)
3) Pager: background spill/prefetch + tests (asha/pager)
4) Integration tests + benchmark harness updates (asha/bench)
5) Docs and config + perf tuning (asha/docs)
review_comments: Liam Chen (reviewer): Nice end-to-end approach. Two asks: include guardrails for CPU/IO (rate limits) and ensure compaction doesn't induce long GC pauses in host memory. Can we add a backpressure metric?

Asha Patel (author): Added compaction_rate_limit and io_budget knobs; instrumentation added as runtime.kv.compaction.backpressure_ratio metric. Also limited compaction slices to 100ms per iteration to avoid long pauses.

Marina Ortiz (reviewer): Eviction scoring looks good. Please add a short comment explaining why fragmentation-weight is capped at 0.6; also add test for eviction ordering when fragmentation and recency disagree.

Asha Patel (author): Added unit test 'evictor_respects_fragmentation_vs_recency' and an inline comment. Fragmentation cap chosen empirically to avoid over-prioritizing compaction for short-lived shards.

Devin Park (SRE): CI failure observed on first run (integration timeout). Reran with increased test timeout and the integration bench passed. Please confirm memory limits for the maintenance pool in Dedicated configs.
Asha Patel (author): Increased maintenance pool limits in deploy/config/kv_compaction.toml and documented recommended Dedicated values in docs/kv-cache.md.
Priya Nair (approver): Verified manual playbook on a staging Dedicated cluster. Observed ~3x reduction in fragment-induced page faults in the simulated long-context workload. Approving to merge.
Merge-bot: PR merged by squash after CI green and approvals.
perf_summary: Staging benchmark with mixed short/long context workload (1k concurrent streams, 20% long-context) shows: p50 latency +0.2% (within noise), p95 latency -6.8%, p99 latency -12.3%, page-fault rate -68% for high-fragmentation shards, and OOM events went from 7/day to 0 in 72h run with default knobs.
testing: Unit tests for compaction correctness and eviction ordering added; integration bench simulates 24h of mixed workload and verifies no regressions in token-serving latency. CI includes a smoke test to ensure maintenance pool can't starve token threads.
rollout_and_monitoring: Feature gated; rollout steps: 1) enable on low-traffic Dedicated pools for 48h, monitor runtime.kv.fragmentation_ratio, runtime.kv.page_faults, runtime.kv.compaction.backpressure_ratio 2) if stable, expand to more pools and enable pager prefetch window 3) enable on Hosted incremental regions. Added dashboards and alerts for fragmentation_ratio>0.35 sustained or compaction.backpressure_ratio>0.7.
release_notes:
- Added adaptive in-place compaction to reduce KV cache fragmentation
- New eviction heuristic that accounts for fragmentation and re-population cost
- Background spillover pager with async prefetch to reduce miss latency
- New runtime knobs and telemetry for tuning compaction and spill IO
notes: This change targets memory management in the KV cache and should reduce tail latency and OOM frequency for workloads with large, variable-length contexts. Watch compaction CPU/IO during the initial rollout.
references: SUP-2091: customer report - repeated page faults
